extracted.intended_audience: news organizations, journalists, editors, publishers, and platform partners (also informative to the general public)
extracted.subtask_description: A set of eight transparency standards (Trust Indicators) for news organizations to disclose information that builds credibility and trust — covering funding, ethics, authorship, sourcing, methods, local knowledge, diversity, and audience feedback. Intended to guide newsrooms and platforms in how to present the provenance and process behind news stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust Indicators (overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Trust Indicators are the first global transparency standard that helps people know who and what is behind a news story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They are built from public input and core journalism values and are presented as eight core disclosures readers deserve: policies to ensure honesty, accuracy and fairness; commitments to own up to mistakes; details about ownership; information on a journalist’s expertise; and more. Use these indicators to build credibility, strengthen audience relationships, and enable platforms to surface reliable news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Who funds the site? What is its mission? What standards and ethics guide the process of gathering news? What happens if a journalist has ties to the topic covered?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose site funding and mission statements; publish standards and ethics guiding newsgathering; explain conflict-of-interest policies and how journalist ties to covered topics are handled. Make organizational policies visible so readers can judge potential influences on coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalist Expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Who made this? Are there details about the journalist, including contact information, areas of knowledge and other stories they’ve worked on?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide author bylines with contact details, beats/areas of expertise, and links to prior relevant reporting to help readers assess the reporter’s qualifications and background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of Work
rubrics_metrics.description: What is this? Do you see story labels with clear definitions to distinguish opinion, analysis, and advertiser (or paid) content from news reports?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly label the type of content (news, opinion, analysis, sponsored/advertiser content) with definitions so readers can immediately understand the nature and purpose of a piece. Avoid mixing formats without clear labeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: References
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the source? Does the site tell you where it got its information? For investigative, controversial, or in-depth stories, are you given access to the original materials behind the facts and assertions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite sources and provide links or access to original materials, documents, datasets, or recordings when feasible—especially for investigative or controversial reporting—so readers can verify claims and understand evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Why was it a priority? For investigations, in-depth or controversial stories, why did they pursue the topic? How did they go about the process?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the rationale for pursuing the story and the methods used (interviews, data analysis, FOIA requests, on-the-ground reporting, etc.). Transparency about methods helps readers evaluate rigor and potential limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locally Sourced
rubrics_metrics.description: Do they know the community? Was the reporting done on the scene? Is there evidence of deep knowledge about the local situation or community?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate whether reporting was conducted locally or on the scene and demonstrate knowledge of the community. Local sourcing and context should be evident to show depth and credibility in place-based reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diverse Voices
rubrics_metrics.description: What are the newsroom’s efforts and commitments to bring in diverse perspectives across social, ideological and demographic differences? Are some communities or perspectives included only in stereotypical ways, or even completely missing?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document newsroom commitments and concrete efforts to include a range of perspectives. Assess and avoid tokenizing or stereotypical inclusion; disclose how sources and viewpoints were selected to show representativeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actionable Feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: What does the site do to engage your help in setting coverage priorities, asking good questions and finding the answers, holding powerful people and institutions accountable and ensuring accuracy? Can you provide feedback that might provoke, alter or expand a story?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide mechanisms for audience engagement and feedback (commenting, contact forms, corrections procedures, editorial input channels) and make clear how public input can influence coverage or corrections. Encourage and facilitate actionable participation from readers.
